title: Songs by artist
scenario: Songs come in as (artist, title) pairs. I need, per artist, the list of their songs.

intro.job: Songs come in as (artist, title) pairs. I need, per artist, the list of their songs.

idea.rule: To group, keep one list per key and append to it — assigning a new list throws the old one away.
idea.detail: groups[artist] = [title] makes a brand-new one-song list every time — the songs already collected for that artist are thrown away. setdefault(artist, []) hands back the list that's already there (or makes an empty one the first time), and .append(title) adds to it — so the list grows instead of restarting.

model_restatement: Group the titles by artist — one list per artist, in the order the songs came in.

clarify.question: What if there are no songs?
Does order matter?
clarify.answer: Yes — keep the songs in the order they came in.

clarify.question: What if the same song appears twice for one artist?
clarify.answer: Then it appears twice in their list.

clarify.question: Do you want counts, or the titles?

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: Make an empty dict. For each song, put the title in that artist's list. Print it.

checkpoints.prompt: With the fix — after iteration 3, what is groups?

why_line: groups[artist] = [title] makes a fresh one-song list every time — ana's 'blue' is thrown away when 'gold' arrives.

explain.rule: Assign replaces: the third song hands ana a brand-new list ['gold'] — and 'blue', collected two turns ago, is gone.
explain.bridge: So how do you keep the list that's already there and add to it?

fix.rule: setdefault(artist, []) hands back ana's list — or an empty one the first time — and .append adds to it.

walk.gloss: Get that artist's list — or an empty one — and add this title.

alternatives.note: Say the empty list out loud first — also fine.

alternatives.code:
from collections import defaultdict
groups = defaultdict(list)
for artist, title in songs:
    groups[artist].append(title)
print(dict(groups))
alternatives.note: Let the dict supply the empty list for you.

hints: After iteration 3, does ana still have 'blue'?
groups[artist] = [title] starts a new list — it doesn't add to the old one.

follow_up.prompt: The same song twice for one artist: [['ana', 'blue'], ['ana', 'blue']] — what gets printed?

checkpoint.prompt: With the same song twice, what gets printed?

follow_up.fix_hint: Nothing to change — grouping keeps every song, even a repeat.

one_liner: To group, keep one list per key and append to it — assigning a new list throws the old one away.
